pairs.question: Ad ultimum quid facturi erunt?
pairs.answer: Dicent quoniam necessitate compulsi nolentes uolentesque humiliauerunt se ad nequissimi irnperatoris uoluntatem.
pairs.derivation: Authorial rhetorical question 'what will they do in the end?' immediately answered by 'They will say that, compelled by necessity, willing and unwilling, they submitted to the will of the most wicked emperor.' Answer is the single following sentence; nothing cut at start; the next paragraph begins a new topic (Boamundus' oath) so the window ends at the full stop.

pairs.question: Tam fortes et tam duri milites, cur hoc fecerunt?
pairs.answer: Propterea igitur, quia multa coacti erant necessitate.
pairs.derivation: Authorial rhetorical question 'so strong and so hardy soldiers, why did they do this?' answered directly by 'For this reason, therefore, because they were constrained by much necessity.' The answer is the closing sentence of the paragraph; the question follows narration of the oath sworn to Boamundus, but stands alone with its referent ('this' = swearing the oath) clear; window ends the paragraph.

pairs.question: Et quis poterat numerare tantam Christi militiam?
pairs.answer: Nullus ut puto tot prudentissimos milites nec antea uidit nec ultra uidere poterit.
pairs.derivation: Authorial rhetorical question 'And who could number so great an army of Christ?' answered by 'No one, I think, has ever seen so many most prudent soldiers before, nor will be able to see hereafter.' The answer ('Nullus...') is the contiguous following sentence and is the end of the paragraph; nothing cut.
